appraisal_events.evidence: les jugements que la duchesse porta ensuite sur Rachel furent en eux-mêmes médiocres
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly assesses the duchess's opinions about Rachel as intellectually mediocre in themselves, valuable only as symptoms of time's passage.

appraisal_events.evidence: tous les gens prétendus d'avant-garde, comme ma nouvelle cousine, dit-elle en montrant ironiquement la princesse de Guermantes... l'auraient laissée crever de faim sans daigner l'entendre
appraisal_events.explanation: The duchess mockingly singles out the princesse de Guermantes as a pretended avant-gardist who would have let Rachel starve, but this claim is part of the duchess's self-glorifying anecdote that the narrator has already flagged as mediocre and unreliable.

appraisal_events.evidence: Gilberte... avait voulu éviter un conflit avec sa tante au sujet de Rachel. Elle avait bien fait
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly endorses Gilberte's prudence in avoiding a conflict with the duchess over defending Rachel.

status_effects.explanation: Her judgments and self-narrated anecdotes about discovering Rachel are framed by the narrator as mediocre and historically unreliable, undercutting her credibility as an arbiter of taste even though her social standing itself is untouched.
She is cast, via the duchess's mocking anecdote, as a false avant-gardist who failed to recognize Rachel's talent early, though the reliability of this characterization is undercut by its source.
The narrator commends her prudent avoidance of a conflict with her aunt over defending Rachel.

ambiguities: The princesse de Guermantes referenced here is the former Mme Verdurin (remarried into the Guermantes family); the passage itself notes this dual identity ('qui, pour Mme de Guermantes, restait Mme Verdurin'). The blame in S2 is scored against 'princesse de Guermantes' as the name directly indicated in the scene, but could equally be read as targeting the Verdurin identity.

The duchess's claim to have 'launched' Rachel and her jab at the princesse de Guermantes are delivered within a monologue the narrator has already characterized as mediocre and self-serving, so the reliability of the blame directed at the princesse is inherently uncertain.
